headline: One example, please.
body: When an explanation loses you, ask, “Could you show me what that would look like in an ordinary situation?” Try explaining the example back in your own words. If it still does not make sense, ask about the part that does not. The nodding can wait.

headline: Put her name back in.
body: The next time you pass along a useful idea, name the woman who gave it to you and what she contributed. “Maya found a simpler way to book the hall” tells people more than “We sorted it.” Check that you are not sharing something she meant to keep private.

headline: Keep the sentence that sounds like you.
body: Choose a short, non-private message you have already written. Ask your AI tool for a plainer version, then compare the two. Keep one change that makes your meaning clearer; reject one that changes your tone or adds a fact. You do not owe the machine a full acceptance speech.
